reason: E1 shows coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced in a W-based RHEA and enhance strength/ductility, but it provides no evidence on radiation tolerance or defect sink behavior. E2 discusses He irradiation tolerance in compositionally complex alloys but does not mention nanoprecipitates or aging treatments. Thus, the core mechanistic premise linking nanoprecipitates to improved radiation tolerance is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced in refractory high-entropy alloys via controlled aging.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as effective defect sinks for irradiation-induced point defects and clusters.
Defect sink action reduces He bubble nucleation/growth and dislocation loop formation.
Reduced defect accumulation mitigates irradiation embrittlement and preserves ductility/strength.
The approach is applicable to additively manufactured, initially single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys.
